# Tobit Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_014_page_001.jpg

---

**14:1** And Tobit ended the-words of praise. And he-was fifty-eight years [old] when he-lost his-eyesight, and after eight years he-received it [back], and he-gave-alms and continued to-fear the-Lord his-God and to-give-thanks to-him.

**14:2** And when he-was-grown very-old, he-called his-son and the-six-sons of his-son and said to-them, "My-child, take your-sons.

**14:3** Behold, I-have-grown-old and am ready to-depart from life. Go to Media, my-child, for I-trust all the-words of Nahum the-prophet concerning Nineveh: that all the-things will-be-fulfilled and will-overtake Assyria and Nineveh, even all that the-prophets of Israel spoke, whom God sent.

**14:4** None of those-words will-fall short; all things will-take-place at their-appointed-times. And in Media it-will-be safer than in Assyria and Babylon. For I-know and I-believe that all the-things God spoke will-be-fulfilled and will-come-to-pass; and not one word of the-prophecies will-fail.

**14:5** And all our-brothers who-dwell in the-land of Israel will-be-scattered and taken-captive from the-good-land, and all the-land of Israel will-become a-waste-land, and Samaria and Jerusalem will-become a-waste-land, and the-house of God will-be-in-sorrow and will-be-burned for a-time.

**14:6** "But God will-again-have-mercy on-them and will-bring-them back to the-land of Israel, and they-will-rebuild the-house, but not as the-former-one, until the-time-when the-times-of the-age are-fulfilled. And after these-things they-all will-return from their-captivity and will-rebuild Jerusalem in-honor, and the-house of God will-be-rebuilt in-it as the-prophets of Israel spoke concerning it.

**14:7** And all the-nations in the-whole earth will-turn and will-fear God truly, and all will-leave their-idols, who-lead-astray them erroneously, and will-bless the-God-of-the-ages in-righteousness.

**14:8** All the-sons of Israel who-will-be-saved in those-days, remembering God truly, will-be-gathered-together and will-come to Jerusalem and will-dwell forever in the-land of Abraham with-safety, and it-will-be-given-over to-them. And those-who-love God truly will-rejoice, and those-who-commit sin and unrighteousness will-be-absent from all the-earth.

**14:9** "Now, my-sons, I-command you: serve-God faithfully and do what-is-pleasing before him; and your-sons also — command them to-do righteousness and eleēmosyna, and to-be-mindful of God and to-bless his-name at-every-time with-sincerity and with all their-strength.

**14:10** And now, my-child, leave Nineveh, for what Nahum said will-surely-come-to-pass. But go to Media, for it [will be] safer there. From my-youth I-trusted Ahikar, and he-helped me until my-old-age. Do you remember what he-did to-the-man Nadan who [was] his-brother's-[son]? He-drew-him down into-the-earth, while he-himself came-up into-the-light. Ahikar gave eleēmosyna and escaped the-death-trap Nadan had-set for-him; but Nadan fell-into the-trap of death and it-destroyed him.

**14:11** So now, my-children, see what eleēmosyna does and what unrighteousness does: it kills! But now my-soul departs."

**14:12** And they-laid-him upon his-bed, and he-died and was-buried honorably.

**14:13** And when Anna his-mother died, Tobias buried-her with his-father. Then Tobias-with his-wife and his-children went-away to Ecbatana to Raguel his-father-in-law.

**14:14** And he-grew-old honorably, and he-buried his-parents-in-law honorably, and he-inherited their-estate and the-estate of his-father Tobit.

**14:15** And he-died in Ecbatana of Media, being ninety-nine years [old]. And he-saw and he-heard of the-destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus had-taken-captive; and before his-death he-rejoiced over Nineveh.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

Codex Sinaiticus gives Tobit's age at blindness as 58, total lifespan as 112 (the numbers are reconstructed: 58 + 8 years blind + 46 more years = 112). Tobias dies at 99 in Sinaiticus. The Vaticanus recension gives different figures (Tobit 158 years, Tobias different). I follow Sinaiticus (GII) throughout.

Verse 3: The prophet cited is Nahum, not Jonah (though both prophesied against Nineveh). Sinaiticus reads *Nahoum* clearly. The prophecy referenced is likely Nahum 1–3, predicting Nineveh's total destruction. This is the only named prophetic citation in Tobit.

Verse 10: The Ahikar story (*Ahiqar*) is a reference to a separate ancient Near Eastern wisdom tale — the story of the wise scribe Ahikar and his ungrateful nephew Nadan. Tobit was apparently a character in versions of that story; here the cross-reference establishes the moral point about *eleēmosyna*.

*Eleēmosyna* is preserved in transliteration in vv. 10 and 11 to highlight its structural function: the final moral of the entire book hangs on this word.

Verse 15: Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus (*Nabouchodonosor kai Achoueros*) as destroyers of Nineveh is historically confused (Nineveh was destroyed by the Medes and Babylonians under Nabopolassar and Cyaxares, 612 BCE). The author may be working from a different historical tradition or using these names typologically.

— EMET
